# v1.4.0 — Skills you can write, and a name that is no longer an identity

You can now write your own skills inside the app, and edit any installed one without losing it to the next update. Two skills that share a name stop being treated as one skill — which they never were. And the whole app is now reachable from the keyboard.

Underneath, this is also the largest structural pass the project has had: every module in both the Rust backend and the frontend was reorganised, and that work surfaced several bugs that were quietly losing data. Those are the fixes worth reading.

> This release includes everything from 1.3.0, which was an internal version and never published.

---

## ✍️ Write your own skills

Two ways in, both producing a **local** skill that belongs to you.

**The builder** — *Skills → Create skill*. A form for the metadata an agent reads and a full-height editor for the instructions, so you never have to hand-write frontmatter YAML. One misplaced comma there and the file stops parsing; the form can't produce one.

**Editing what you already have** — open any installed skill and its name and its whole `SKILL.md` are editable.

**A skill from a repository is never overwritten.** Its global copy is a mirror of what the repo publishes and gets replaced wholesale on reinstall, so saving over it would lose your work at the first update. Saving produces a **local copy** instead, and the original keeps receiving updates. For your own skills you choose each time: save in place, or branch off a copy. Without a name of your own, the copy takes a `-local` suffix.

Both paths enter through the same install pipeline as everything else, so a new skill inherits slug resolution, the per-repository bucket and the database record — rather than being a second way in that drifts from the first.

**From the CLI**

```
ccode skill show <name|id>                 metadata plus the SKILL.md itself
ccode skill new  <name>                    [--description] [--categories a,b]
                                           [--agents a,b] [--file <path> | --content "..."]
ccode skill edit <name|id>                 [--file | --content] [--name] [--copy]
```

`--file` is read by the CLI binary itself, so the path is relative to where *you* ran the command, not to where the app is running.

---

## 🪪 A name is no longer an identity

Two skills can share a name and be completely different things by different authors — and in a directory like skills.sh that happens *within the same repository*, because one "repo" lists many publishers. The name was standing in as identity in five places, and each one was its own bug:

| Where | What went wrong |
|---|---|
| **Marketplace** | A set of names meant installing `testing` from one repo marked every other repo's `testing` as installed, and greyed out the button for a skill you didn't have |
| **Database** | The row only recorded which repo a skill came from. Now it records **which entry** of it (`origin_skill_id`, schema v8) — for skills.sh the entry is `owner/repo/slug`, which carries the author inside it |
| **Reinstalling** | Accumulated `testing`, `testing-2`, `testing-3` from the same source. Now it updates in place, keeping the row id so everything attached to it survives |
| **Sessions** | Reopening a session could silently mount a same-named skill by a different author. Now you're always told when the exact copy is gone, and substitution only happens when there is exactly one candidate |
| **The CLI** | An ambiguous name took whichever row SQLite returned first. Now it's an error that lists the candidates with their author and repo |

Broken-symlink warnings also identify a skill by id rather than by name.

And so you can tell them apart at a glance: the **author** is now extracted from the frontmatter (and from the publisher on skills.sh), travels with the marketplace entry, and is shown both in the marketplace grid and in your installed list.

<details>
<summary><b>What happens to skills you already installed</b></summary>

Rows from before this release have no origin entry recorded. They get linked when you refresh the repository they came from — and **only when the match is unambiguous**. Guessing would reintroduce the exact bug this fixes, so an ambiguous row is left alone rather than attached to the wrong origin.

</details>

## ⌨️ Keyboard navigation

| | |
|---|---|
| `Ctrl+H` | Home |
| `Ctrl+E` | Sessions |
| `Ctrl+K` | Skills |
| `Ctrl+M` | Marketplace |
| `Ctrl+G` | Settings |
| `Ctrl+Tab` · `Ctrl+Shift+Tab` | Next / previous tab, wrapping at both ends |

**Each section shortcut is a toggle.** Already in Marketplace? `Ctrl+M` takes you back to your terminal. Without that they'd be one-way: fast to leave your work, a click to return.

They work while you're typing inside an agent, which is the whole point — and that has a price worth stating plainly. `Ctrl+M` *is* Enter and `Ctrl+H` *is* Backspace at the terminal level, and `Ctrl+E` / `Ctrl+K` are readline editing keys. Those four stop reaching the agent. In practice Enter and Backspace have their own keys and still work; what you actually lose is emacs-style editing. The full list and this caveat live in **Settings → Keyboard shortcuts**.

---

## 🛟 Fixes that were losing data

These are the ones to read. All four were found during the restructure.

**Updating the app could delete every saved tab.** A database without the `tabs.opened_at` column was migrated by *recreating the table*. The schema version now lives in `PRAGMA user_version` and each migration runs once and is recorded, instead of being re-derived on every launch by probing which columns exist. The column is now added; the pre-v3 model is set aside as `*_legacy_v2` rather than dropped.

**Moving a tab to another window lost half of it.** The transfer payload listed its fields by hand, and the four that weren't on the list vanished without an error:

- `historyId` → closing it in the destination archived a *new* history entry
- `prelaunch` → the tab arrived without its pre-launch chain
- `titleIsCustom` → a title you set by hand stopped being protected
- `openedAt` → became "now", and since it's the time floor for session discovery, it discarded the transcript of a process that had been alive for hours — the tab lost its session id, and with it the ability to resume

The whole tab now travels, so adding a field to it can't reopen the hole. The detach path also stopped using `localStorage` as a mailbox with no addressee: it creates the window, waits for it to announce it's ready, and sends the tab by a directed event.

**Closing a tab could freeze the entire app.** Archiving resolved the session title while holding the SQLite lock — and for OpenCode that means running `opencode session list` and waiting. The whole database was blocked for about a second per tab, and forever if that process hung, since everything goes through one connection. That work now happens *before* the lock is taken, and every external command runs under a timeout that kills it if it doesn't answer.

**Installing a skill could install the wrong folder.** With several candidate directories, the code fell through to `.first()` — and `read_dir` has no guaranteed order, so it installed a skill at random under another one's name.

---

## 🐛 More fixes

| | |
|---|---|
| A TUI installed in a path with spaces, or a flag with a quoted value, arrived split into pieces | the command is now parsed respecting quotes |
| Session history was de-duplicated on every single launch | correlated subqueries over the whole history, every time. Now it runs once, latched in settings |
| The `+` dialog re-rendered every time any terminal reported a pty id | 31 store subscriptions took the whole store instead of the field they used |
| Home and the `+` dialog disagreed on which agents to list | both now derive the list from one place |
| A screen reader announced "btn.delete" | two translation keys used as `aria-label` existed in neither language |
| Packaging the `.deb` aborted | Tauri's bundler treats every entry in `src/bin/` as a binary to ship, so a folder holding the CLI's tests made it look for an executable that doesn't exist |

---

## 🧱 Under the hood

Nothing here changes what the app does. It changes how fast the next thing can be built — and it's why the fixes above exist at all.

<details>
<summary><b>The Rust backend</b></summary>

Every `mod.rs` is now purely declarative — module declarations and re-exports, no logic — so the file tree is the map of the code. The four largest files were split by responsibility:

| Was | Became |
|---|---|
| `db.rs` (2461 lines) | `connection` · `schema` · `seeds` · `models` · `queries/` grouped by domain |
| `skills/mod.rs` (2208) | `types` · `frontmatter` · `files` · `settings` · `install` · `store` · `links` · `sessions` |
| `marketplace/mod.rs` (1273) | one file per source: `local` · `github` · `skillssh`, plus `types` · `registries` |
| `ipc/commands.rs` (1096) | `commands/` per domain, and the TCP server out to `server.rs` |

Tests moved out of the logic they cover into one `test.rs` per module, and now build their database from the **real schema** instead of a hand-written copy — which is how several test-only bugs turned out to be actual bugs. Startup moved out of `lib.rs` into `app/`. **184 tests.**

Dead code went with it: the four tmux commands and their module, `list_skill_usage`, `reorder_registries`, `db_close_workspace_windows`, `db_get_open_window_labels`.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>The frontend</b></summary>

From folders by kind (`pages/`, `components/`, `store/`, `lib/`) to folders by domain. Each feature now holds its own page, components, store, typed IPC layer and tests:

```
app/        the shell: router, top bar, exit dialogs
shared/     what belongs to no feature
features/   tabs · terminal · workspaces · sessions · skills · marketplace
            agents · accounts · prelaunch · orchestrator · settings
```

**No component writes the name of a backend command in a string any more.** That was a contract nothing verified: renaming a command in Rust broke nothing until a user pressed the button. Every call now goes through its feature's `ipc.ts` — zero loose `invoke` calls remain.

The frontend had no tests and no runner. It now has Vitest and **81 tests** over the pure logic, in a `tests/` folder inside each feature.

</details>

## 📦 Install

Grab the installer for your platform below. Your data is kept: the database migrates itself, and workspaces, tabs and sessions saved with 1.2.0 open normally.

Skills installed before this release keep working. They pick up their origin entry — and with it their author badge — the next time you refresh the repository they came from.
